It addresses the storage inefficiency of standard hash encodings by enabling high-ratio compression (up to 1,529×) while maintaining high fidelity, positioning it as a viable solution for HPC-scale scientific volume data [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method addresses storage inefficiency by enabling high-ratio compression (up to 1,529×) while maintaining high fidelity, positioning it as a viable solution for HPC-scale scientific volume data. The evidence confirms: 1) The improved APMGSRN achieved 1,529× compression with 49.04 dB PSNR (high fidelity) on a large asteroid dataset (111.71 GB). 2) The text explicitly contrasts this with standard hash encoding, noting that while standard encoding has lower compression ratios, the improved method achieves high-ratio compression. 3) The text mentions DVNR validating INR methods at HPC scale (up to 512 MPI ranks), and the improved APMGSRN is presented in the context of these advancements for large-scale data (asteroid dataset). Although the specific '1,529×' figure is attributed to the improved APMGSRN and the 'HPC scale' validation is explicitly linked to DVNR in the text, the claim broadly attributes these capabilities to the subject discussed in S1 (which covers both methods as part of the progression of INR compression techniques). The facts in the claim (1,529x compression, high fidelity, HPC context) are all present in the evidence.
supported
